tex_content.label: infprod2
tex_content.html:
Every three-dimensional $\kappa $-solution is exactly one of:

  1. positively curved at every time;

  2. the product of shrinking round $S^2$’s with a line;

  3. a flow on a line bundle over $\Ar P^2$ having a finite cover of type (2).

Proof

\sketch If positive curvature fails, the strong maximum principle gives a one- or two-sheeted cover splitting into a round surface flow and a flat circle or line. A fixed circle factor violates non-collapsing as $t\to -\infty $. The remaining factor is a line; a further double cover replaces $\Ar P^2$ by $S^2$, yielding (2) or (3).

□
